messages:
morgan: Quick heads-up — I'm seeing a measurable perf regression when switching to FlashAttention v3 for some long-seq traffic. Happens only with paged-attn + KV-reuse + autobatcher enabled. Repro attached (tiny script + config).

santiago: Ugh. Can you paste the repro snippet and the perf numbers?

morgan: Repro is simple. Run a workload with seq_len=4096, batch size 6, kv_reuse=true, autobatcher=on. At ~step 20 the 95th latency jumps ~25%. Paste: ```python
# minimal repro loop
for i in range(100):
    model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=512, use_cache=True)
```

anya: Do you have a profile (nvprof/torchprof) or the runtime trace? Even a flamegraph would help.

morgan: Attached CPU/gpu profiles in the PR comment. Short summary: kernel selection switches from fa_v2_small_seq path to fa_v3_paged on that traffic, and we see repeated KV cache materialization in host memory between microbatches.

kevin: @morgan can you confirm feature flags in play? Is this behind the new runtime flag we rolled out yesterday?

morgan: Yes. The rollout flag is enable_flash_v3_global=true + fwk.autobatcher=adaptive. We only enabled v3 for a small set of hosts.

nina: If KV cache gets materialized per microbatch that could explain the extra copies. Are we evicting/rebuilding the paged KV shards?

morgan: Exactly. Trace shows repeated calls to page_fetch() for the same key ranges across minibatches, instead of reusing pinned pages. Looks like the KV cache warm path isn't marking pages as hot when autobatcher groups requests with shifting offsets.

perf-bot: deploy-bot: Canary hosts with flag enable_flash_v3_global=true rolled to 4/10; latency alert triggered on host infra-12 at 12:03:22 UTC.

santiago: Two angles: 1) short-term rollback or gated fallback for paged-attn when kv_reuse + autobatcher both true; 2) deeper fix in the paged-attn cache hotmarking logic.

anya: For short-term mitigation we could add an fflag fallback that forces fa_v2_small_seq for seq_len>=2048 when kv_reuse=true. That keeps v3 available for other workloads.

kevin: Agree. Also add a telemetry counter for repeated page_fetches per request id so we can target the hosts.

morgan: I can land the fflag today: "ff_attn_v3_paged_kv_autobatch_fallback" default=on. Plan: roll to canary, watch 95th latency, then ramp.

nina: For the long-term fix I'll pair with @anya on reworking the hotmarking: ensure pinned pages survive autobatcher shuffles and add a lightweight LRU guard to avoid page churn.

anya: We'll need tests: synthetic microbatch ordering tests that simulate offset shifts and ensure no extra page_fetch after warmup. I'll add a unit test in runtime/tests/paged_kv_reuse_test.py.

perf-bot: perf-regression-bot: baseline comparison queued for run 2761002000; includes fa_v2 vs fa_v3 combinations and kv toggles.

santiago: Also important: double-check kernel chooser heuristics — maybe selection criteria currently prefer v3 because of some synthetic bench even though real paged workloads behave differently. Add an extra heuristic for "paged_kv_hotness" to bias toward v2 when hotness low.

morgan: Good call. I'll instrument the chooser to emit chooser.reason per request so we can verify.

kevin: Ops/rollout checklist: 1) land fflag + telemetry, 2) canary to 2 hosts, 3) run perf-regression-bot, 4) if green ramp to 30%, else rollback. Keep config quick-toggle.

nina: For the patch I'll prepare a changelog entry: "Fix: paged KV reuse with autobatcher to avoid redundant page materialization (v3)" and link to the issue.

anya: Estimated timeline: fflag + telemetry in a few hours, tests & hotmarking follow-up PR by EOD tomorrow.

morgan: Thanks all — I'll post the canary results in this thread. If anyone sees new alerts ping here. :white_check_mark:
